what_it_does: 3D chiplet stacking lets designers assemble powerful processors from multiple smaller chips stacked vertically with solder bumps, reducing power and latency. However, the interposer (the middleman chip) traditionally routes signals for one specific chip combination, wasting the interposer if you want to use different top chips. SHINSAI is a reusable interposer built in 28-nanometer technology with a programmable fabric (a reconfigurable routing network) that connects to different top chips. It includes 512 megabits of on-interposer SRAM (ultra-fast memory) for buffering data between stacked chips, with programmable pathways to route this data flexibly to whoever needs it.
